statements.status_notes: When asked to use a .netrc file for credentials and to follow HTTP redirects, curl could leak the password used for the first host to the followed-to host under certain circumstances. This flaw only manifests itself if the .netrc file has a default entry that omits both login and password.
statements.impact_statement: The password leak needs a libcurl-based transfer that reads credentials from a .netrc file whose default entry omits both login and password, and then follows an HTTP redirect to another host. curl is present in the image but nothing in the runtime path invokes it, the only binary that links libcurl is the curl command-line tool itself, the JRE does not link libcurl (Liquibase's HTTP traffic goes through the JDK HTTP client), and lpm is a statically linked Go binary, so no libcurl transfer ever happens in Liquibase Secure. Fixed in Ubuntu curl 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.23 (jammy; Liquibase Secure 5.0.0 and 5.0.1 shipped 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.20 and 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.21) and 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.8 (noble; Liquibase Secure 5.0.2 through 5.1.0 shipped 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.6); Liquibase Secure 5.1.1 and later ship 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.8 or newer.

statements.status_notes: curl's WebSocket code did not update the 32-bit mask pattern for each new outgoing frame as the specification says. Instead it used a fixed mask that persisted and was used throughout the entire connection. A predictable mask pattern allows for a malicious server to induce traffic between the two communicating parties that could be interpreted by an involved proxy (configured or transparent) as genuine, real, HTTP traffic with content and thereby poison its cache. That cached poisoned content could then be served to all users of that proxy.
statements.impact_statement: curl's WebSocket client reused one 32-bit mask for every outgoing frame of a connection, so a malicious WebSocket server could induce traffic that an intermediate proxy might cache as genuine HTTP; upstream fixed it in 8.16.0 and considers only 8.11.0 through 8.15.0 affected, because WebSocket was experimental before 8.11.0. curl is inherited from the Ubuntu base image and nothing in the runtime path uses it: the container's build steps download with wget, its entrypoint runs the Liquibase CLI, the only binary that links libcurl is the curl command-line tool itself, the JRE does not link libcurl (Liquibase's HTTP and TLS traffic goes through the JDK), and lpm is a statically linked Go binary. A source review found no reference to libcurl or to WebSocket transfers through curl. Ubuntu lists the 22.04 package (7.81.0, in the 5.0.0 and 5.0.1 images) as not affected because the code is not present there, and published the fix for 24.04 as 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.7 (USN-8062-1). Docker images 5.0.2 through 5.1.0 carry the unfixed 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.6; 5.1.1 and later carry 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.8 or newer.

statements.status_notes: When doing multi-threaded LDAPS transfers (LDAP over TLS) with libcurl, changing TLS options in one thread would inadvertently change them globally and therefore possibly also affect other concurrently setup transfers. Disabling certificate verification for a specific transfer could unintentionally disable the feature for other threads as well.
statements.impact_statement: The global TLS-option leak needs a libcurl-based application that performs multi-threaded LDAPS transfers while changing TLS options per transfer. curl is present in the image but nothing in the runtime path invokes it, the only binary that links libcurl is the curl command-line tool itself, the JRE does not link libcurl (Liquibase's HTTP traffic goes through the JDK HTTP client), and lpm is a statically linked Go binary, so no libcurl transfer ever happens in Liquibase Secure. Fixed in Ubuntu curl 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.22 (jammy; Liquibase Secure 5.0.0 and 5.0.1 shipped 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.20 and 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.21) and 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.7 (noble; Liquibase Secure 5.0.2 through 5.1.0 shipped 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.6); Liquibase Secure 5.1.1 and later ship 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.8 or newer.

statements.status_notes: When an OAuth2 bearer token is used for an HTTP(S) transfer, and that transfer performs a cross-protocol redirect to a second URL that uses an IMAP, LDAP, POP3 or SMTP scheme, curl might wrongly pass on the bearer token to the new target host.
statements.impact_statement: The bearer-token leak needs a libcurl-based HTTP(S) transfer that uses an OAuth2 bearer token and then follows a cross-protocol redirect to IMAP, LDAP, POP3 or SMTP. curl is present in the image but nothing in the runtime path invokes it, the only binary that links libcurl is the curl command-line tool itself, the JRE does not link libcurl (Liquibase's HTTP traffic goes through the JDK HTTP client), and lpm is a statically linked Go binary, so no libcurl transfer ever happens in Liquibase Secure. Fixed in Ubuntu curl 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.22 (jammy; Liquibase Secure 5.0.0 and 5.0.1 shipped 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.20 and 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.21) and 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.7 (noble; Liquibase Secure 5.0.2 through 5.1.0 shipped 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.6); Liquibase Secure 5.1.1 and later ship 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.8 or newer.

statements.status_notes: When doing TLS related transfers with reused easy or multi handles and altering the CURLSSLOPT_NO_PARTIALCHAIN option, libcurl could accidentally reuse a CA store cached in memory for which the partial chain option was reversed. Contrary to the user's wishes and expectations. This could make libcurl find and accept a trust chain that it otherwise would not.
statements.impact_statement: libcurl could reuse a cached CA store whose CURLSSLOPT_NO_PARTIALCHAIN setting differed from the current transfer's when an application reused easy or multi handles for TLS transfers and changed that option between them; upstream fixed it in 8.18.0, the affected range is 7.87.0 through 8.17.0, and the curl command-line tool itself is not affected, only applications that call the libcurl API. curl is inherited from the Ubuntu base image and nothing in the runtime path uses it: the container's build steps download with wget, its entrypoint runs the Liquibase CLI, the only binary that links libcurl is the curl command-line tool itself, the JRE does not link libcurl (Liquibase's HTTP and TLS traffic goes through the JDK), and lpm is a statically linked Go binary. A source review found no reference to libcurl or CURLSSLOPT_NO_PARTIALCHAIN. Ubuntu lists the 22.04 package (7.81.0, in the 5.0.0 and 5.0.1 images) as not affected because the code is not present there, and published the fix for 24.04 as 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.7 (USN-8062-1). Docker images 5.0.2 through 5.1.0 carry the unfixed 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.6; 5.1.1 and later carry 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.8 or newer.

statements.status_notes: When doing SSH-based transfers using either SCP or SFTP, and setting the known_hosts file, libcurl could still mistakenly accept connecting to hosts not present in the specified file if they were added as recognized in the libssh global known_hosts file.
statements.impact_statement: The host-key bypass needs a libcurl SCP or SFTP transfer that sets its own known_hosts file. curl is present in the image but nothing in the runtime path invokes it, the only binary that links libcurl is the curl command-line tool itself, the JRE does not link libcurl (Liquibase's HTTP traffic goes through the JDK HTTP client), and lpm is a statically linked Go binary, so no libcurl transfer ever happens in Liquibase Secure. Fixed in Ubuntu curl 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.22 (jammy; Liquibase Secure 5.0.0 and 5.0.1 shipped 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.20 and 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.21) and 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.7 (noble; Liquibase Secure 5.0.2 through 5.1.0 shipped 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.6); Liquibase Secure 5.1.1 and later ship 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.8 or newer.

statements.status_notes: When doing SSH-based transfers using either SCP or SFTP, and asked to do public key authentication, curl would wrongly still ask and authenticate using a locally running SSH agent.
statements.impact_statement: The SSH-agent fallback needs a libcurl SCP or SFTP transfer that requests public-key authentication. curl is present in the image but nothing in the runtime path invokes it, the only binary that links libcurl is the curl command-line tool itself, the JRE does not link libcurl (Liquibase's HTTP traffic goes through the JDK HTTP client), and lpm is a statically linked Go binary, so no libcurl transfer ever happens in Liquibase Secure. Fixed in Ubuntu curl 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.22 (jammy; Liquibase Secure 5.0.0 and 5.0.1 shipped 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.20 and 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.21) and 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.7 (noble; Liquibase Secure 5.0.2 through 5.1.0 shipped 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.6); Liquibase Secure 5.1.1 and later ship 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.8 or newer.

statements.status_notes: A use-after-free vulnerability exists in libcurl when an application configures an HTTP/2 stream-dependency tree via CURLOPT_STREAM_DEPENDS or CURLOPT_STREAM_DEPENDS_E, subsequently invokes curl_easy_reset(), and finally terminates the handle with curl_easy_cleanup(). During this final cleanup phase, libcurl attempts to access and modify an internal structure that was already freed during the reset operation.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports curl 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.10, below Ubuntu's fixed 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.11, but this issue affects applications that configure libcurl stream dependencies and then reset and clean up the same handle. Liquibase Secure's build path uses wget for downloads, not curl, and a review of the secure-image build and stock runtime path found no use of curl or the affected libcurl APIs.

statements.status_notes: Using libcurl to do a transfer to a specific HTTP origin with Digest authentication and then changing the origin to a different one for a second transfer while reusing the same handle causes libcurl to wrongly pass on the Authorization header field meant for the first origin to the second. This flaw does not affect the curl command-line tool.
statements.impact_statement: This flaw is in libcurl's handle-reuse behavior: reusing the same handle for Digest-authenticated transfers to two different origins can leak the first origin's Authorization header to the second. Per curl's own advisory, this does not affect the curl command-line tool at all — only applications that reuse a libcurl handle across origins. The container's build steps use wget, not curl, for downloads, and the runtime entrypoint execs only the Liquibase CLI — a source review found no invocation of curl anywhere in this repository's Docker build or runtime path. This OS package's version is not pinned by this repository — it tracks whatever the unversioned eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble base image tag resolves to at build time. Confirmed by pulling the current base image directly and checking installed package versions (not from repo-pinned config), it ships curl 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.13, newer than the fixed release, as additional defense-in-depth.

statements.status_notes: A flaw in the libcurl SASL negotiation for LDAP authentication allows an incomplete handshake sequence to be misinterpreted as a successful cryptographic verification. An attacker executing a Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attack can inject a premature or shortcut response that bypasses complete peer validation.
statements.impact_statement: This flaw requires an application to use libcurl's SASL negotiation for LDAP authentication. Liquibase Secure's runtime process tree never links against libcurl and never performs LDAP authentication via libcurl; curl ships only as an inherited base-image package and is never invoked at container runtime.

statements.status_notes: A flaw in libcurl's handling of HTTP/2 Server Push streams, when the parent handle is set to share connections with other handles, can lead to use-after-free in the cleanup process.
statements.impact_statement: This use-after-free requires an application to configure libcurl handles to share connections while processing HTTP/2 Server Push streams. Liquibase Secure's runtime process tree never links against libcurl; curl ships only as an inherited base-image package and is never invoked at container runtime.

statements.status_notes: libcurl can incorrectly reuse an existing Negotiate-authenticated connection for a later request to the same server with different credentials, causing the request to run under the wrong authenticated identity.
statements.impact_statement: The wrong-connection reuse needs a libcurl-based application that performs Negotiate (SPNEGO) authenticated transfers with different credentials over one connection pool. curl is present in the image but nothing in the runtime path invokes it, the JRE does not link libcurl (Liquibase's HTTP traffic goes through the JDK HTTP client), and lpm is a statically linked Go binary, so no libcurl transfer ever happens in Liquibase Secure. Fixed in Ubuntu curl 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.23 (jammy, shipped by Liquibase Secure 5.0.0 and 5.0.1) and 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.8 (noble); Liquibase Secure 5.0.2 through 5.1.0 shipped 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.6, and Liquibase Secure 5.1.1 and later ship 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.8 or newer.

statements.status_notes: A flaw in libcurl makes it wrongly reuse an HTTP connection setup for a given hostname using Negotiate authentication, when the initial request is done using empty credentials. This can make user B's request get sent over user A's previously authenticated connection.
statements.impact_statement: This flaw is a libcurl API-level connection-reuse bug: an application linked against libcurl must issue Negotiate-authenticated requests with empty initial credentials for the vulnerable connection-pooling logic to trigger. The Liquibase Secure container entrypoint execs only the Liquibase Java CLI; a review of the JVM's own native library dependencies and the container's runtime entrypoint found no linkage against libcurl anywhere in the process tree. curl ships only as an inherited base-image package and is never invoked at container runtime.

statements.status_notes: When an OAuth2 bearer token is used for an HTTP(S) transfer, and that transfer performs a redirect to a second URL, curl could leak that token to the second hostname under some circumstances. If the redirected host has information in the used .netrc file, curl would pass on the bearer token set for the first host also to the second one.
statements.impact_statement: This CVE requires a libcurl-based application to perform an OAuth2 bearer token transfer that follows a redirect while consulting .netrc entries for the redirected host. Liquibase Secure's stock container does not invoke curl or link against libcurl in its own build or runtime path, so the vulnerable token-forwarding path is not reachable from Liquibase Secure.

statements.status_notes: curl would wrongly reuse an existing HTTP proxy connection doing CONNECT to a server, even if the new request uses different credentials for the HTTP proxy. The proper behavior is to create or use a separate connection.
statements.impact_statement: This CVE requires a libcurl-based application to reuse an HTTP proxy CONNECT connection while changing proxy credentials between requests. Liquibase Secure's stock container does not invoke curl or link against libcurl in its own build or runtime path, so the vulnerable proxy connection-reuse path is not reachable from Liquibase Secure.

statements.status_notes: A connection requiring TLS can incorrectly reuse an existing unencrypted connection from the same connection pool. If an initial transfer is made in clear-text via IMAP, SMTP, or POP3, a subsequent request to that same host bypasses the TLS requirement and transmits data unencrypted.
statements.impact_statement: This CVE requires a libcurl-based application to reuse a connection pool across clear-text and TLS-required IMAP, SMTP, or POP3 transfers. Liquibase Secure's stock container does not invoke curl or link against libcurl in its own build or runtime path, so the vulnerable connection- pool reuse path is not reachable from Liquibase Secure.

statements.status_notes: libcurl might in some circumstances reuse the wrong connection when asked to do an authenticated HTTP(S) request after a Negotiate-authenticated one, when both use the same host.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports curl 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.20, below Ubuntu's fixed 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.24, but this issue requires a libcurl-based application to reuse a connection after a Negotiate-authenticated request while switching credentials for a later authenticated request to the same host. Liquibase Secure's stock container uses wget for its own downloads and executes the Liquibase Java CLI at runtime, and a focused review found no Negotiate-authenticated libcurl flow, connection-pool reuse, or curl option handling in the product runtime path.

statements.status_notes: libcurl might in some circumstances reuse the wrong connection for SMB(S) transfers.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports curl 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.20, below Ubuntu's fixed 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.24, but this issue requires a libcurl-based application to perform SMB(S) transfers while reusing live connections across requests that target different shares on the same server. Liquibase Secure's stock container uses wget for its own downloads and executes the Liquibase Java CLI at runtime, and a focused review found no SMB, libcurl connection-pool reuse, or curl option handling in the product runtime path.

statements.status_notes: curl might erroneously pass on credentials for a first proxy to a second proxy.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports curl 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.20, below Ubuntu's fixed 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.24, but this issue requires a libcurl-based application to follow a cross-scheme redirect while using distinct proxies per scheme and proxy credentials on the first proxy. Liquibase Secure's stock container uses wget for its own downloads and executes the Liquibase Java CLI at runtime, and a focused review found no proxy-authenticated libcurl flow, redirect-following, or curl option handling in the product runtime path.

statements.status_notes: Using libcurl, when a custom Host: header is first set for an HTTP request and a second request is subsequently done using the same easy handle but without the custom Host: header set, the second request would use stale information and pass on cookies meant for the first host in the second request.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports curl 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.20, below Ubuntu's fixed 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.24, but this issue requires a libcurl-based application to reuse the same easy handle across multiple HTTP requests while first setting a custom Host header and later omitting it. Liquibase Secure's stock container uses wget for its own downloads and executes the Liquibase Java CLI at runtime, and a focused review found no custom Host header handling, cookie replay path, or libcurl easy-handle reuse in the product runtime path.

statements.status_notes: When asked to both use a .netrc file for credentials and follow HTTP redirects, libcurl could leak the password used for the first host to the followed-to host under certain circumstances.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports curl 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.20, below Ubuntu's fixed 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.24, but this issue requires a libcurl-based application to combine .netrc credential loading with HTTP redirect following. Liquibase Secure's stock container uses wget for its own downloads and executes the Liquibase Java CLI at runtime, and a focused review found no libcurl, .netrc, or redirect-handling path in the container build or runtime entrypoint.

statements.status_notes: Successfully using libcurl to do a transfer over one HTTP proxy with Digest authentication and then changing the proxy host for a second transfer while reusing the same handle can cause libcurl to pass the Proxy-Authorization header intended for the first proxy to the second.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports curl 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.20, below Ubuntu's fixed 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.24, but this issue requires a libcurl-based application to reuse the same handle across multiple proxy hosts with Digest authentication enabled. Liquibase Secure's stock container uses wget for downloads and executes the Liquibase Java CLI at runtime, and a focused review found no proxy-authenticated libcurl flow, Digest-proxy handling, or curl handle reuse path in the container build or runtime entrypoint.

statements.status_notes: When CURLOPT_PINNEDPUBLICKEY is configured alongside options that disable standard peer verification (CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER = 0 and CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYHOST = 0), libcurl fails to enforce public key pinning on connections established without a presented server certificate, allowing unauthenticated connections to succeed when they should be rejected.
statements.impact_statement: This flaw requires an application to configure libcurl with CURLOPT_PINNEDPUBLICKEY alongside disabled peer verification options. Liquibase Secure's runtime process tree never links against libcurl; curl ships only as an inherited base-image package and is never invoked at container runtime.

statements.status_notes: When libpsl support is enabled, libcurl fails to enforce the Public Suffix List boundary check when processing a Set-Cookie header where the Domain attribute explicitly matches an origin host that is itself a public suffix. Instead of coercing it into a strict host-only cookie, libcurl saves the cookie with wildcard domain scope, inappropriately including it in subsequent outbound requests or HTTP redirects to arbitrary sibling subdomains under the same public suffix.
statements.impact_statement: This flaw requires an application to build libcurl with libpsl support and process attacker-controlled Set-Cookie responses. Liquibase Secure's runtime process tree never links against libcurl; curl ships only as an inherited base-image package and is never invoked at container runtime.

statements.status_notes: A new transfer that uses STARTTLS to upgrade the connection might reuse an existing live connection even though the TLS configuration mismatches and the connection should not have been reused.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports curl 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.20, below Ubuntu's fixed 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.25, but this issue requires a libcurl-based application to upgrade a connection with STARTTLS and then incorrectly reuse a live connection whose TLS settings no longer match. Liquibase Secure's stock container uses wget for its own downloads and executes the Liquibase Java CLI at runtime, and a focused review found no STARTTLS, curl connection-pool, or libcurl TLS-reuse path in the container build or runtime entrypoint.

statements.status_notes: libcurl might reuse the wrong connection when asked to perform Negotiate-authenticated requests, even when those requests are set to use different services.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports curl 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.20, below Ubuntu's fixed 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.25, but this issue requires a libcurl-based application to reuse pooled connections across Negotiate-authenticated requests that change the target service. Liquibase Secure's stock container uses wget for downloads and executes the Liquibase Java CLI at runtime, and a focused review found no Negotiate-authenticated libcurl flow, service- aware connection reuse, or curl handle pool in the container build or runtime entrypoint.

statements.status_notes: Setting `CURLOPT_AWS_SIGV4` to NULL does not disable SigV4 authentication, contrary to expectations and documentation. A subsequent transfer on the same handle still sends an `Authorization: AWS4-HMAC-SHA256` header to whatever URL is set next, leaking state information.
statements.impact_statement: Setting CURLOPT_AWS_SIGV4 to NULL did not disable SigV4 authentication on a reused libcurl handle, so a later transfer on the same handle could still send an AWS4-HMAC-SHA256 Authorization header to a different URL. Upstream rates it low and lists the affected range as 7.75.0 up to the fixes in 8.14.3, 8.16.2, 8.20.2 and 8.22.0. curl is inherited from the Ubuntu base image and nothing in the runtime path uses it: the container's build steps download with wget, its entrypoint runs the Liquibase CLI (and lpm only when INSTALL_MYSQL is set), the only binary that links libcurl is the curl command-line tool itself, the JRE does not link libcurl (Liquibase's HTTP and TLS traffic goes through the JDK), and lpm is a statically linked Go binary. A source review found no reference to libcurl or its API (including CURLOPT_AWS_SIGV4). Ubuntu fixed the 24.04 package in 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.16 and the 22.04 package in 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.30; the scanner reported 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.15.

statements.status_notes: An HTTP proxy can trick libcurl into sending the origin's credentials (Basic password, or a Negotiate/Kerberos ticket) to the proxy itself, by answering the `CONNECT` tunnel request with 401 `WWW-Authenticate:` instead of the expected 407 `Proxy-Authenticate:`.
statements.impact_statement: An HTTP proxy could make libcurl send the origin's credentials (Basic password or a Negotiate/Kerberos ticket) to the proxy by answering a CONNECT tunnel request with 401 WWW-Authenticate instead of 407 Proxy-Authenticate. Upstream rates it low and lists the affected range as 7.10.8 up to the fix in 8.23.0. curl is inherited from the Ubuntu base image and nothing in the runtime path uses it: the container's build steps download with wget, its entrypoint runs the Liquibase CLI (and lpm only when INSTALL_MYSQL is set), the only binary that links libcurl is the curl command-line tool itself, the JRE does not link libcurl (Liquibase's HTTP and TLS traffic goes through the JDK), and lpm is a statically linked Go binary. A source review found no reference to libcurl or its API. Ubuntu fixed the 24.04 package in 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.16 and the 22.04 package in 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.30; the scanner reported 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.15.

statements.status_notes: Importing an `includeSubDomains` parent HSTS entry before a longer-lived child entry silently drops the child. Consequently, when the parent expires, the child's valid HSTS policy is lost, causing curl to issue unencrypted HTTP requests rather than upgrading to HTTPS.
statements.impact_statement: When an HSTS cache file imports an includeSubDomains parent entry before a longer-lived child entry, the child is dropped, so after the parent expires curl can issue plain HTTP requests for the child host. Upstream rates it low and lists the affected range as 8.11.0 up to the fixes in 8.14.3, 8.16.2, 8.20.2 and 8.23.0. curl is inherited from the Ubuntu base image and nothing in the runtime path uses it: the container's build steps download with wget, its entrypoint runs the Liquibase CLI (and lpm only when INSTALL_MYSQL is set), the only binary that links libcurl is the curl command-line tool itself, the JRE does not link libcurl (Liquibase's HTTP and TLS traffic goes through the JDK), and lpm is a statically linked Go binary. A source review found no reference to libcurl or its API (including HSTS cache files). Ubuntu fixed the 24.04 package in 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.16 and the 22.04 package in 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.30; the scanner reported 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.15.

statements.status_notes: An authenticated HTTPS origin can supply an HSTS `max-age` value that the parser accepts, but time serialization later fails to process. On 64-bit systems, extreme max-age values compute an absolute expiry within standard time integer limits that exceeds calendar time structure bounds. During cache saves, the original HSTS file is truncated before writing a temporary replacement; when serialization fails, the temporary file is deleted, leaving an empty or partial cache. Because the save error is silently ignored during cleanup, curl exits successfully despite the data loss.
statements.impact_statement: An HTTPS origin can send an extreme HSTS max-age value that libcurl accepts but cannot serialize, which truncates the saved HSTS cache file and silently loses its entries. Upstream rates it low and lists the affected range as 8.2.0 up to the fixes in 8.14.3, 8.16.2, 8.20.2 and 8.23.0. curl is inherited from the Ubuntu base image and nothing in the runtime path uses it: the container's build steps download with wget, its entrypoint runs the Liquibase CLI (and lpm only when INSTALL_MYSQL is set), the only binary that links libcurl is the curl command-line tool itself, the JRE does not link libcurl (Liquibase's HTTP and TLS traffic goes through the JDK), and lpm is a statically linked Go binary. A source review found no reference to libcurl or its API (including HSTS cache files). Ubuntu fixed the 24.04 package in 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.16; the 22.04 package does not contain the affected code. The scanner reported 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.15.

statements.status_notes: Enabling `CURLOPT_CRLF` causes curl to advertise the raw input byte count in the `IMAP APPEND {N}` literal while transmitting line-ending expanded data. The server reads only N bytes for the payload, causing the remaining overflow bytes to be interpreted and executed as pipelined IMAP commands within the authenticated session.
statements.impact_statement: With CURLOPT_CRLF enabled, libcurl advertised the raw byte count in an IMAP APPEND literal while sending CRLF-expanded data, so the extra bytes could be read by the server as pipelined IMAP commands. Upstream rates it low and lists the affected range as 7.30.0 up to the fixes in 8.14.3, 8.16.2, 8.20.2 and 8.22.0. curl is inherited from the Ubuntu base image and nothing in the runtime path uses it: the container's build steps download with wget, its entrypoint runs the Liquibase CLI (and lpm only when INSTALL_MYSQL is set), the only binary that links libcurl is the curl command-line tool itself, the JRE does not link libcurl (Liquibase's HTTP and TLS traffic goes through the JDK), and lpm is a statically linked Go binary. A source review found no reference to libcurl or its API (including CURLOPT_CRLF or IMAP). Ubuntu fixed the 24.04 package in 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.16 and the 22.04 package in 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.30; the scanner reported 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.15.

statements.status_notes: A flaw in curl's cookie parsing logic allows a malicious HTTP server to set "super cookies" that bypass the Public Suffix List check. This enables an attacker-controlled origin to inject cookies that curl subsequently scopes and transmits to unrelated third-party domains.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports curl 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.20, below Ubuntu's fixed 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.25, but this issue requires Liquibase Secure to act as a curl HTTP client that parses and stores attacker-controlled cookies and later reuses them against unrelated domains. Liquibase Secure's build downloads use wget, and its stock runtime path invokes Liquibase rather than curl, so curl's cookie parsing, Public Suffix List, and cookie jar handling are not exercised.

statements.status_notes: The curl logic that works with SASL authentication could end up cleaning up the GSASL context twice without clearing the pointer in between, making it free() the same pointer twice.
statements.impact_statement: This CVE requires a libcurl-based application to use SASL authentication and exercise the GSASL cleanup path on a curl handle. Liquibase Secure's stock container does not invoke curl for its own build or runtime operations, and a source review found no references to GSASL, SASL-authenticated curl flows, or libcurl option usage in the product runtime path. curl is inherited from the base image only, so the vulnerable libcurl path is not reachable from Liquibase Secure.

statements.status_notes: When reusing a libcurl handle for sequential transfers driven by environment-variable proxy configuration, libcurl fails to clear the proxy authentication state between requests. Specifically, if the initial transfer authenticates against proxyA using Digest auth, a subsequent transfer routed through proxyB erroneously leaks the Proxy-Authorization header intended solely for proxyA.
statements.impact_statement: This CVE requires a libcurl-based application to reuse a handle across sequential transfers that pick up proxy settings from environment variables and negotiate Digest authentication to multiple proxies. Liquibase Secure's stock container does not invoke curl for its own build or runtime operations, and a source review found no references to proxy-authenticated libcurl flows or related curl option usage in the product runtime path. curl is inherited from the base image only, so the vulnerable libcurl path is not reachable from Liquibase Secure.

statements.status_notes: libcurl would reuse a previously created connection even when some mTLS config related option had been changed that should have prohibited reuse. libcurl keeps previously used connections in a connection pool for subsequent transfers to reuse if one of them matches the setup. However, some TLS settings related to client certificates were left out from the configuration match checks, making them match too easily. In particular options related to the private key.
statements.impact_statement: This CVE requires a libcurl-based application to reuse pooled connections while changing mutual-TLS client-certificate settings. Liquibase Secure's stock container does not invoke curl for its own build or runtime operations, and a source review found no references to libcurl mutual-TLS option usage or connection-pool handling in the product runtime path. curl is inherited from the base image only, so the vulnerable libcurl path is not reachable from Liquibase Secure.

statements.status_notes: When an FTP wildcard `LIST` operation fails, libcurl omits the restoration path meant for successful listings, leaving the write callback set to the internal listing parser and the write callback data pointing directly to the easy handle. Subsequent reuse of this handle triggers an immediate crash, and cloning it via `curl_easy_duphandle()` copies this corrupted state into the duplicate. If the original handle is subsequently freed, executing a transfer on the cloned handle causes a heap use-after-free read against the dangling handle reference; alternatively, reusing the original or cloned handle while changing only `CURLOPT_WRITEDATA` (and omitting `CURLOPT_WRITEFUNCTION`) results in type confusion, forcing the internal parser to interpret incoming server response bytes into memory at the application-supplied write data pointer.
statements.impact_statement: After a failed FTP wildcard LIST, libcurl left its internal listing parser installed as the write callback, so reusing or duplicating the handle could crash, read freed memory or write server data to an application pointer. Upstream rates it low and lists the affected range as 7.21.0 up to the fix in 8.23.0. curl is inherited from the Ubuntu base image and nothing in the runtime path uses it: the container's build steps download with wget, its entrypoint runs the Liquibase CLI (and lpm only when INSTALL_MYSQL is set), the only binary that links libcurl is the curl command-line tool itself, the JRE does not link libcurl (Liquibase's HTTP and TLS traffic goes through the JDK), and lpm is a statically linked Go binary. A source review found no reference to libcurl or its API (including FTP wildcard transfers). Ubuntu fixed the 24.04 package in 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.16 and the 22.04 package in 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.30; the scanner reported 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.15.

statements.status_notes: libcurl's TFTP state machine fails to validate state transitions against the requested transfer direction, accepting opening server responses for both reads and writes interchangeably. A malicious TFTP server can respond to a download request in a way that forces the client into transmit mode, prompting libcurl to consume and transmit data from the handle's persistent `CURLOPT_READDATA` pointer, including data remaining from unrelated prior operations, such as an HTTP POST request executed on a reused handle.
statements.impact_statement: libcurl's TFTP state machine did not check the transfer direction, so a malicious TFTP server could switch a download into an upload and make libcurl send data from the handle's CURLOPT_READDATA source, including data left over from earlier transfers on a reused handle. Upstream rates it low and lists the affected range as 7.15.0 up to the fixes in 8.14.3, 8.16.2, 8.20.2 and 8.23.0. curl is inherited from the Ubuntu base image and nothing in the runtime path uses it: the container's build steps download with wget, its entrypoint runs the Liquibase CLI (and lpm only when INSTALL_MYSQL is set), the only binary that links libcurl is the curl command-line tool itself, the JRE does not link libcurl (Liquibase's HTTP and TLS traffic goes through the JDK), and lpm is a statically linked Go binary. A source review found no reference to libcurl or its API (including TFTP transfers). Ubuntu fixed the 24.04 package in 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.16 and the 22.04 package in 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.30; the scanner reported 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.15.

statements.status_notes: A deeply nested multipart MIME structure constructed via the public API causes a stack overflow in libcurl during normal cleanup operations. An excessive recursion depth within `curl_mime_free` leads to unbounded stack frame allocation during structure traversal, ultimately crashing the host process.
statements.impact_statement: A deeply nested multipart MIME structure built through the libcurl API causes unbounded recursion in curl_mime_free, crashing the process with a stack overflow. Upstream rates it low and lists the affected range as 7.56.0 up to the fixes in 8.14.3, 8.16.2, 8.20.2 and 8.23.0. curl is inherited from the Ubuntu base image and nothing in the runtime path uses it: the container's build steps download with wget, its entrypoint runs the Liquibase CLI (and lpm only when INSTALL_MYSQL is set), the only binary that links libcurl is the curl command-line tool itself, the JRE does not link libcurl (Liquibase's HTTP and TLS traffic goes through the JDK), and lpm is a statically linked Go binary. A source review found no reference to libcurl or its API (including curl_mime_free). Ubuntu fixed the 24.04 package in 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.16 and the 22.04 package in 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.30; the scanner reported 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.15.

statements.status_notes: libcurl could accidentally return a URL for `curl_easy_getinfo()`'s `CURLINFO_EFFECTIVE_URL` option containing credentials, even though neither the URL provided to libcurl nor the redirected URL did.
statements.impact_statement: libcurl could return a URL containing credentials from curl_easy_getinfo with CURLINFO_EFFECTIVE_URL even though neither the original nor the redirected URL contained them. Upstream rates it low and lists the affected range as 7.62.0 up to the fix in 8.23.0. curl is inherited from the Ubuntu base image and nothing in the runtime path uses it: the container's build steps download with wget, its entrypoint runs the Liquibase CLI (and lpm only when INSTALL_MYSQL is set), the only binary that links libcurl is the curl command-line tool itself, the JRE does not link libcurl (Liquibase's HTTP and TLS traffic goes through the JDK), and lpm is a statically linked Go binary. A source review found no reference to libcurl or its API (including CURLINFO_EFFECTIVE_URL). Ubuntu fixed the 24.04 package in 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.16 and the 22.04 package in 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.30; the scanner reported 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.15.

statements.status_notes: When a libcurl-based application performs transfers via SCP:// or SFTP:// and utilizes the CURLOPT_SSH_KEYFUNCTION callback, it may silently accept an untrusted server. This vulnerability occurs when a server presents a host key type that does not match the specific key type already recorded for that host in the known_hosts file. Instead of rejecting the mismatch, the callback mechanism fails to properly enforce the restriction, allowing the connection to succeed without warning and risking a potential man-in-the-middle attack.
statements.impact_statement: This CVE requires a libcurl-based application to perform SCP or SFTP transfers and register the CURLOPT_SSH_KEYFUNCTION callback so host-key validation flows through the vulnerable known_hosts handling. Liquibase Secure's stock container does not invoke curl for its own build or runtime operations, and a source review found no references to SCP, SFTP, CURLOPT_SSH_KEYFUNCTION, or known_hosts callback handling in the product runtime path. curl is inherited from the base image only, so the vulnerable libcurl path is not reachable from Liquibase Secure.
